item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is marginally preferable, but both need contract-driven revisions before merge.","reasons":["Both correctly add the required Upload signature and use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\".","Both violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add, instead duplicating its option handling, request execution, decoding, and missing-data error logic.","Both unnecessarily modify global RawClient retry behavior, changing Files.Add semantics despite the contract requiring Add behavior and retry machinery to remain unchanged.","A's validation is clearer and occurs before option processing, with distinct filename and content errors; B combines both into a less informative error after processing options may already have occurred outside the intended sequence via cfg construction (though not request). More importantly, A's seekability extension falls back to existing behavior when seeking fails, while B introduces new Raw.Do failures for SeekCurrent/SeekEnd and changes ContentLength/transfer behavior for arbitrary io.ReadSeeker values. That makes B's forbidden scope expansion more compatibility-sensitive and risky. (The options point is minor.) Correction: cfg construction itself doesn't necessarily mean option side effects beyond applying options; the primary advantage remains precise errors and less invasive seeker semantics. Both omit the required source-reader failure test; B's os.File retry test is more representative of the report, but it does not outweigh its broader RawClient behavior changes."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, creating duplicate behavior that can drift from the lower-level API.","The RawClient seekable-body replay change is explicitly out of scope and changes retry and reader-closing semantics globally.","No test exercises an io.Reader that returns an error; the retry test uses strings.Reader rather than a forward-only streamed source."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.","RawClient now seeks every eligible body to its end, can reject readers previously accepted, sets ContentLength, and changes reader ownership and retry semantics globally.","Validation returns one generic error for two distinct invalid arguments and occurs only after option processing via newFilesOptions; no source-reader failure test is included."]}
